_comment: TEKS — Social Studies, Grade 7 (Texas History), §113.19. Codes transcribed from the TEA §113.19 rule (2022 adoption). §113.19(c)(3)(C) names the Battle of Gonzales explicitly. Subject to the June 2026 K–8 revision; confirm current numbering.
verificationNote: Wording transcribed from the TEA §113.19 rule (adopted 2022). TRANSITION: revised K–8 social studies TEKS adopted June 2026 will renumber Grade 7; confirm which version applies to your school year.

7.3(C).text: explain the issues surrounding significant events of the Texas Revolution, including the Battle of Gonzales, the siege of the Alamo and all the heroic defenders who gave their lives there, the Constitutional Convention of 1836, Fannin's surrender at Goliad, and the Battle of San Jacinto

7.3(A).text: trace the development of events that led to the Texas Revolution, including the Fredonian Rebellion, the Mier y Terán Report, the Law of April 6, 1830, the Turtle Bayou Resolutions, and the arrest of Stephen F. Austin

7.20(D).text: identify points of view from the historical context surrounding an event and the frame of reference that influenced the participants

7.20(B).text: analyze information by sequencing, categorizing, identifying cause-and-effect relationships, comparing, contrasting, finding the main idea, summarizing, making generalizations and predictions, and drawing inferences and conclusions

7.23.text: The student uses problem-solving and decision-making skills, working independently and with others (supports the 'could events have gone differently?' analysis)
